newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says it sends fighters to eastern border.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says it sends fighters to eastern border.

text.p: Sudan said on Wednesday that it was sending fighters to the country's eastern border to counter a rebel advance on a key garrison.

"The massive attack by Ethiopia on the east of the country comes within the context of the foreign plots targeting the security, unity and stability of Sudan," Sudanese Defence Minister Lt-Gen Hasan Abdel-Rahman Ali told a women's battalion headed to the operation zone.
He said "the armed forces and all of the Sudanese people are capable of responding to the attack and giving the mercenaries a lesson they would never forget."
Sudanese President Omar Hassan al-Bashir has called for a mobilisation and said the gun would decide the struggle for power in Africa's largest country.

Sudan is mustering recruits to drive back the rebels, northerners and southerners working together in their first combined offensive to overthrow the Islamist government which took power in a military coup in 1989.
Sudanese rebels said on Wednesday they had captured or attacked more army garrisons in the east and were advancing on Damazin.
Sudan state radio reported that convoys and mujahideen, or holy warriors, were headed to the southern Blue Nile town, site of a hydroelectricity plant that supplies Khartoum.
"Damazin is receiving convoys after convoy and mujahideen are on their way to the frontline," the radio said.

It also claimed that Sudan's paramilitary People's Defence Force had inflicted "huge losses in men and materiel" in Chali el Fil, 50 km (30 miles) south of Kurmuk, where the rebels had previously reported military successes.
